1. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests and data records from a plurality of creditors to file bankruptcy documents with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein the bankruptcy documents are specifically formatted proofs of claim documents;
automatically generating the bankruptcy documents with the received data records, wherein the bankruptcy documents are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations and include debtor-specific information and creditor claim amounts;
and
batch filing the bankruptcy documents with the different bankruptcy organizations via automated electronic submission to each organization's filing system.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different courts with different filing system configurations, and wherein the method further comprises automatically adapting the format of each bankruptcy document to comply with the specific filing requirements of each court.

6. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests from a plurality of creditors to file proofs of claims for debts owed by debtors to the creditors with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein each request includes a data record for generating a proof of claim, and wherein the data record includes creditor identification, claim amount, and claim basis information;
automatically generating the proofs of claims with the received data records, wherein the proofs of claims are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations and are formatted according to each organization's specific requirements;
and
batch filing the proofs of claims with the different bankruptcy organizations via automated electronic submission systems.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different bankruptcy courts having different filing system configurations, and wherein the method further comprises automatically reformatting each proof of claim to comply with each court's specific filing format requirements.
